subStrands.name: Computing Devices: Pre-computing Age to 20th Century

objectives.description: Features, components and uses of early computing devices (pre-computing age, 19th century): Abacus; Slide Rule; Napier's bone; Pascal's calculator; Leibnitz multiplier; Jacquard loom; Charles Babbage's analytical engine; Hollerith Census Machine; Burrough's Machine. Contribution of each founder to modern computers. Trend of development in computing devices from one to the other.

Features, components and uses of 20th century computing devices: ENIAC; EDVAC; UNIVAC 1; Desktop Personal Computers; Laptop and Notebook computers; Palmtop. Comparative study of sizes and basic components.

Definition of a computer. Two main constituents of a computer: computer hardware and computer software. Classification and examples of hardware and software. Differences between hardware and software. Functional parts of a computer.
Characteristics of computers: electronic in nature; accuracy; speed; interactive etc.
Data and Information: definition and examples of data and information; differences between data and information.

Definition and examples of input devices. Use of keyboard, mouse, scanner, joystick, light pen. Classification of keys on the keyboard: function, numeric, alphabetic, cursor keys. Features, function and operation of the mouse. Differences in keyboard, mouse, light pen and scanner.

Definition and examples of output devices: monitor, printer, speaker, plotter – type, features and uses. Differences between input and output devices. Similarities and differences in inkjet, laser and line printers. Examples and types of printers and monitors.
Components of CPU: Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU), Control Unit. Functions of ALU and Control Unit. Combination of the CPU and Memory Unit as system unit.
Types of Memory Unit: Primary and Secondary memory. Components of Primary memory: ROM and RAM. Differences and uses of ROM and RAM. Physical identification of RAM and ROM devices.

Examples of Secondary memory devices: floppy disk, hard disk, compact disk (CD), flash disk, digital video disk (DVD). Unit of storage: bits, nibble, bytes, kilobytes, megabytes, gigabytes, terabytes. Interconversion of units of storage. Comparative study of auxiliary storage devices in respect of size, speed and technology.

Definition, types, uses and symbols of standard logic gates: AND, NOT, OR. Logic equations for AND, NOT, OR gates. Construction of truth tables for standard logic gates. Differences between AND, NOT, OR gates.
NAND and NOR as alternative logic gates. Construction of truth table for NAND and NOR. Construction of a simple comparator with XOR (Exclusive OR) and NOR gate.
Definition and types of software: system software and application software. Differences between system and application software.
System software and their examples: Operating System (e.g. MS Windows); Translator (e.g. Compiler); Tools/Utility (e.g. Antivirus).
Examples of Operating Systems: MS Windows; Linux; UNIX; MS-DOS. Operating systems of phones, iPad and other computerized devices e.g. Android, Blackberry.
Examples of Translators: Assemblers; Compilers; Interpreters. Differences among the translators.
Examples of Utility Programs: Editor; Anti-virus.

Definition, types, examples and function of Operating System: Graphic User Interface (GUI) e.g. MS Windows, Linux; Command line e.g. MS-DOS, UNIX. Differences between GUI and Command line Operating Systems.

Definition and types of application software. Common Application Packages and their examples: Word processing (MS Word); Spreadsheet (MS Excel); Database (MS Access); Graphics. Differences between user application program and application packages.
Packages for specific purposes: accounting software; payroll program; banking software; education management software; statistical packages; hospital management software.
Definition and examples of word processing and word processors: MS Word; Wordstar; WordPerfect. Features of word processing programs. Application areas: office, publishing, journalism, education.

Features of MS Word. Steps in activating and exiting MS Word. Basic operations: create, edit, save, retrieve, print, close. Further operations: move, copy, cut, use of different types and sizes of fonts, formatting, justifying, search/explore, spell checking, file merging.
Definition and examples of spreadsheet programs: VisiCALC; MS Excel; SuperCALC; Autocad. Features of spreadsheet programs. Application areas: accounting, statistical calculation, student results.
Features of MS Excel environment: status bar, menu bar, formula bar. Definition of basic terms: worksheet, workbook, cells, cell ranges. Data types in Excel: number, labels, formula.

Basic operations in Excel: data entry, saving, retrieve, copy, move. Arithmetic calculations using formula and built-in functions (sum, average, etc.). Additional operations: editing, formatting, printing, drawing charts (pie chart, histogram, bar chart).
Definition of database and database packages. Examples: Dbase IV; Foxbase; MS Access; Oracle. Basic terms: file, record, field, key.
Types of database organisation methods and their features: hierarchical; network; relational. Features of database format: files designed as tables; tables comprise rows and columns.

Steps in creating a database: define the structure; indicate field type (numeric, character, data, text); enter data; save data. Basic operations on a database: searching, modifying, sorting, reporting, selecting, inserting.

Definition of graphics. Examples of graphics packages: Paint; Harvard graphics; Photoshop; CorelDraw. Features in activating and exiting CorelDraw. Simple design using CorelDraw: business card, school logo, national flag, invitation card, certification.

Definition of presentation package. Examples: MS PowerPoint. Features of PowerPoint environment. Steps in activating and exiting PowerPoint. PowerPoint operations: create new presentation, insert pictures/text/graphs, animated contents, add new slide, save, run slide show, print, close presentation.
Definition of terms: computer file, record, field, data item. Types of data item: numeric, alphabetic, alphanumeric.

File structure organisation: Data item → record → file → database. Types of file organisation: serial, sequential, index, random. Differences among the organisation methods. Methods of accessing files: serial, sequential, random.
File classification: master file, transaction file, reference file. Criteria for classifying files: nature of content (program and data), organisation method, storage medium.
Basic operations on computer files: file, delete, retrieve, insert, copy, view, update, open, close. File processing using BASIC programming.

Effect of file insecurity: data loss, data corruption, data becomes unreliable. Causes of data loss: over-writing, inadvertent deletion. Methods of file security: use of backup, use of antivirus, password, proper labelling of storage devices.
Differences between computer files and manual files. Advantages of computer files: more secure, fast to access. Disadvantages of computer files: expensive to set up, irregular supply of electricity.

Description and types of booting process: cold booting and warm booting. Differences between cold and warm booting. Steps involved in booting a computer and shutting down a computer. Identification of features on a desktop.

Computer data conversion: definition of registers, address, bus. Types and functions of registers: MDR, CIR, SCR. Differences between register and main memory. Steps involved in how a computer converts data to required information (Input-Process-Output). Factors affecting speed of data transfer: bus speed; bus width.

What 'ICT' acronym stands for. Types of ICT: Broadcasting, Telecommunication, Data Network, Information Systems, Satellite Communications. Examples of broadcasting: radio broadcasting, television broadcasting, satellite system. Examples of telecommunication: PSTN (landline), mobile phone systems, CSPT, satellite telephone system, fixed wireless telephone system.

Examples of data networks: Personal Area Network (PAN), Local Area Network (LAN), Metropolitan Area Network (MAN), Wide Area Network (WAN), Internet. Examples of information systems: Data Processing System, Global Positioning System (GPS).
Application areas of ICT: teleconferencing, video conferencing, telecommuting, telecomputing, messaging, information search/retrieval and archival.

ICT-based gadgets and their operations: mobile phones, computers, fax machines, Automated Teller Machines (ATM), dispensing machines, Point of Sale machines, Automated Cash Register (ACR), radio sets, television sets.

Definition of Internet and internet terms: homepage, browse, browser, chatroom, cybercafe, HTTP, HTML, ISP, webpage, website. Types of internet browsers: Internet Explorer, Netscape Navigator, Opera, Firefox, Cometbird. Features of internet browsers: title bar, menu bar, tool bar, address bar.

Types of internet services: electronic mail (e-mail), e-mail discussion group, instant messaging, Telnet, Usenet, File Transfer Protocol (FTP), World Wide Web (www), chatting. Benefits of Internet to society.

Definition of electronic mail. E-mail services: sending/receiving e-mail, chatting. Steps in creating e-mail account and opening mailbox. Features in an e-mail address. Definition and steps involved in chatting.

Definition of a computer network. Types of network: PAN, LAN, WAN, MAN, Internet. Network topology: Star, Bus, Ring. Differences in the various topologies. Network devices: Hub, Modems, Switches, Routers, Network Interface Card (NIC), Bridge. Advantages of networking.

Introduction to World Wide Web (WWW): what WWW acronym stands for; brief history; basic terminologies (website, webpage, homepage, protocol). Protocol: HTTP, HTML. Uses/benefits of www. Navigating through websites. Difference between e-mail and website address. Software for web development.

Types of Network Cables and Connectors: cables (twisted pair, coaxial, fibre optic, telephone); connectors (RJ45, RJ11, T-connectors). Types of Computer Cables and Connectors: power cables, data cables (printer cable, USB, monitor cable, serial cable); male and female connectors.

Programming language: definition, examples, levels and features. Levels and examples: Machine Language (ML) e.g. 100011001; Low Level Language (LLL) e.g. Assembly Language; High Level Language (HLL) e.g. BASIC, C++, FORTRAN. Comparison, advantages and disadvantages of ML, LLL and HLL.

High Level Languages: definition and examples. Classification as scientific, general-purpose, business, AI, string processing language (SPL). Features of BASIC, C, PASCAL, COBOL – comparative study. Other programming languages such as Java, Python.

Definition of algorithm and flowchart. Functions of algorithm. Characteristics of algorithm: finite, effective, unambiguous. Writing algorithm for: computing average of a given set of numbers; evaluation of equations; computing the first ten odd numbers.
Flowchart symbols: I/O, Process, Decisions. Use of each flowchart symbol. Drawing flowchart diagrams for given programming problems.
What BASIC acronym stands for. BASIC characteristics. Types of data: variable, constant/literal, numeric, string/alphanumeric.
BASIC Statements: INPUT; PRINT, LPRINT; LET; END; REM; READ; DATA. Arithmetic operators (-,+,*,/). Arithmetic expressions and their evaluation.
Simple BASIC programs: calculate area of triangle, area of rectangle, average of 3 numbers. Running simple programs on the computer.

Built-in functions in BASIC: SQR(X), INT(X), SIN(X), ABS(X), RND(X), COS(X), TAN(X), LOG(X), EXP(X). BASIC notation of mathematical expressions. BASIC programs to find square roots, cosines, tangents and plot sine wave curve.

Additional BASIC Statements: DIM Statement; FOR-NEXT statement; WHILE-END statement. Defining one-dimensional array using DIM statement. Operating on array elements: input, output, arithmetic operations. Write BASIC programs to store vectors, calculate means, calculate areas of rectangles, compute sum of first 100 integers. Numbers of iterations should not exceed eight (8).

Definition of program. Characteristics of a good program: accuracy, readability, maintainability, efficiency, generality, clarity. Precautions in developing a program. Steps in program development: problem definition, problem analysis, flow charting, desk checking, program coding, program compilation, program testing/debugging, program documentation. Description of each stage. Examples of interpreted program (BASIC) and compiled program (COBOL, FORTRAN).

Definition of system development cycle. Description and stages in system development cycle: preliminary study, feasibility, investigate study, analysis, design, implementation, maintenance, study review. Description of each stage and diagram of system development cycle.

Sources of security breaches: virus, worms and Trojan horses (definition and effects); poor implementation of network; poor implementation or lack of ICT policies; carelessness in giving out personal information online; hackers and spammers (definitions).

Preventive measures: use of antivirus software (e.g. Norton, McAfee, Avast); use of firewall (definition and explanation); exercising care in giving out vital and personal information; encryption (definition); proper network implementation and policies; using sites with web certificates; exercising care in opening e-mail attachments.
Legal issues: copyright (software copyright); ownership rights to text, images, audio, video; privacy of audio and video software; cyber crimes including identity theft, internet fraud, hacking.
